content.text:
Below are summaries of 8 consecutive chunks of a long story, given in document order (chunk 1 came first in the story, chunk 8 came last):

Chunk 1 summary: Coningsby discovers his mother’s miniature in a banker’s box and meets Edith Millbank in Paris. Misreading Sidonia’s friendship with Edith, he leaves, but later learns the truth. He and Edith fall in love at Hellingsley; Millbank forbids their marriage because of his feud with Lord Monmouth. Coningsby rejects his grandfather’s demand to contest Darlford, is disinherited, and enters the Temple to study law. After Millbank nominates him, Coningsby wins Darlford and marries Edith at Millbank; Flora later leaves him her fortune. Meanwhile, Lord Monmouth separates from Lucretia and dies, leaving his estate to Flora. A separate narrative follows pirate Captain Flint, who operates from a crystal cave with Lightfoot and Black Bill. Haunted voices and apparitions frighten the crew, while Flint plans further piracy and disguises attacks as the work of another pirate.

Chunk 2 summary: Captain Flint’s pirate crimes are exposed when Henry Billings recognizes him and helps capture him at sea. Flint escapes prison, returns to his cave, kills Jones Bradley, and is later torn apart by a bear. Fire Cloud secretly rescues Hellena, Lightfoot, and Black Bill through a hidden passage from the cavern to an Indian village. Billings is mistakenly captured as Flint, delaying his reunion with Hellena, but they eventually return safely to New York. The cave’s “supernatural” noises are explained as echoes produced by Black Bill and Fire Cloud.

The remainder consists of John Evelyn’s diary: observations of London society, religious and political conflict, royal deaths and successions, the Popish Plot, the Monmouth rebellion, persecution of Protestants, James II’s Catholic policies, the imprisonment and acquittal of the bishops, and William of Orange’s invasion and accession.

Chunk 3 summary: The text combines excerpts from several historical works: John Evelyn’s diary (1689–1705), describing political upheaval, religious disputes, wars, weather, scientific and cultural life, family deaths, and the founding of Greenwich Hospital; memoirs of Minnesota’s territorial printers, Civil War service, and St. Paul society; accounts of the battles of Mill Springs and Pittsburg Landing; a young woman’s diaries recording family, weddings, travel, religious life, and her grandmother’s death; and essays comparing Maya, Egyptian, African, Asian, and American cultures, especially writing, mythology, customs, and music. It also includes advertisements, market reports, bibliographical notices, and editorial corrections. Notable movements include Evelyn’s visits to London, Lambeth, Wotton, Deptford, Kensington, Eton, and Greenwich; the diarist’s travels through England, Scotland, Paris, and America; and soldiers’ movements through Kentucky, Tennessee, Mississippi, and the Dakotas.

Chunk 4 summary: The first section surveys medieval and post-medieval musical instruments: lyres, psalteries, harps, rottas, fiddles, organs, wind instruments, bells, carillons, lutes, viols, and related orchestras, emphasizing their evolution, regional variation, and historical evidence.

The novel follows Jessica Lawton’s millinery shop and charitable Girls’ Resting House, Kate Minster’s support, and Horace Boyce’s morally corrupt ambitions. Tenney and Wendover manipulate the Minster fortune through fraudulent industrial schemes, while Reuben Tracy uncovers the conspiracy and helps Kate and Ethel. After the mills close and workers threaten violence, Jessica learns of a mob and seeks Reuben. She finds Horace in a lawyer’s office, then travels with Gedney in a sleigh to Reuben’s mother’s farmhouse, where Reuben is visiting his sick mother.

Chunk 5 summary: Jessica Lawton travels to Reuben Tracy’s mother’s farm, rescues him for the threatened Minster estate, steals Gedney’s affidavits, and leaves the mob at the Minster house. Reuben pacifies the crowd, then learns Jessica has collapsed at General Boyce’s house; dying, she reconciles Horace and Reuben and reveals their child.

Other tales follow Cissy Trixit fleeing her seized Canada City home to find her fugitive father, and Masterton pursuing her through the Sierras. At a fonda, Cota’s horse attacks men, inspiring a ghost legend. On Eureka Mountain, Eugenia falls onto Bray, whose companions discover gold; “Jack” and “Jill” reunite in San Francisco. Miss Trotter’s hotel career and Chris Calton’s failed engagement lead to their love. Lester Kane takes Jennie from Cleveland to New York and Chicago, concealing her daughter Vesta.

Chunk 6 summary: Jennie’s concealed daughter, Vesta, is discovered, forcing her to confess her past to Lester. He brings Vesta into their Chicago apartment, later moves the household to a Hyde Park home, and accepts Jennie’s father Gerhardt there. Social condemnation, family pressure, and his father’s will eventually compel Lester to separate from Jennie so he can reclaim his fortune. Jennie moves with Vesta to a cottage in Sandwood; after Vesta dies of typhoid, Jennie returns to Chicago. Lester, having married Letty Gerald and regained wealth, falls ill in the Auditorium Hotel and summons Jennie, confessing that she was the only woman he truly loved. He dies shortly afterward, while Jennie watches his funeral procession and train depart for Cincinnati. The appended theological chapters explain Baptism, Eucharist, and Confirmation as sacramental unions of matter and spirit, emphasizing their essentials, saving grace, regeneration, adoption, election, communion, and the laying on of hands.

Chunk 7 summary: The text combines several works. A religious manual explains Holy Matrimony, Holy Order, Penance, and Unction, emphasizing consent, Apostolic Succession, clerical roles, confession, absolution, and healing. Historical chapters recount Lord Durham’s Canadian mission, the rebellions of 1837–38, battles at Lacolle and Odelltown, executions, and later reconciliation. Fiction follows Winton’s “S. W. F. Club,” whose members explore the village, visit the manor, picnic at The Maples and an old fort, and prepare to leave for school. Another story describes Minnie’s mischievous pet monkey Jacko. A Cornish travel narrative records visits to the Lizard, Lizard Lights, Marazion, St. Michael’s Mount, Land’s End, Whitesand Bay, Tintagel, and Boscastle. Finally, on the Big Horn Ranch, Allan and Mandy go fishing, rescue an injured Piegan boy, and meet his returning companions.

Chunk 8 summary: Mandy and Allan Cameron rescue a Piegan boy, then learn that the aristocratic Chief Onawata—“Copperhead”—is plotting an uprising. Cameron and Inspector Dickson fail to arrest him at the Piegan camp; Copperhead burns the ranch, but Mandy survives. Cameron later pursues him through Calgary, the Sun Dance Canyon, and Indigenous reserves while Mandy, Moira, Dr. Martin, Smith, and allies support the rebuilding of the ranch. Moira and Martin fall in love; outlaw Raven saves her from a runaway wagon and later dies helping Cameron stop a cattle stampede. During the wider 1885 rebellion, Cameron captures Copperhead after escaping captivity with Jerry. The Police prevent a western Indigenous uprising, while the appended diary shifts abruptly to 1865 American Civil War news, Lincoln’s assassination, Booth’s death, Davis’s capture, church life, and local social observations.

Question: Where is Mary?

People in this story move between rooms over time. If more than one summary states a location for Mary, the correct answer is the LAST one in document order -- ignore earlier ones, they are out of date. Answer with ONLY the room name: no article (a/an/the), no punctuation, no explanation, nothing else. If no summary states a location for Mary, answer NOT FOUND.
